teksten.**Alternatief van [Baseline] - IOS - D -: **Alternative to [Baseline] - IOS - D - Apple Intelligence Permitted** — which sets the same keys to true; assigning both results in a Conflict, after which neither does anything. Siri itself stays on; only Siri on the lock screen is turned off via Restrictions Corporate. Deliberately not: allowappleintelligencereport=false (that report is precisely the transparency about what went to Private Cloud Compute) and forceondeviceonlydictation/-translation (not a generative feature). For devices without enrolment, App Protection has the iOS 26 fields writingToolsConfigurationState and genmojiConfigurationState; they are deliberately not in the phase 1 policy, because this is an organisational decision and App Protection is only one policy for everyone — see RAPPORT.

**Alternative to [Baseline] - IOS - D - Apple Intelligence Restricted.** Before choosing this one, take into account that the ChatGPT integration (externalintelligencesettings_enabled) sends data to an external party; anyone who only wants to allow the on-device features sets externalintelligencesettings_enabled to false in this policy. The per-workspace restriction (allowedworkspaceids) is deliberately not included: it requires a tenant or workspace ID.
teksten.**Alternatief van [Baseline] - MAC - D -: **Alternative to [Baseline] - MAC - D - Apple Intelligence Permitted** — that one sets the same twelve settings to the opposite value. Assigning both results in a Conflict, and then neither does anything. Checked: [Baseline] - MAC - D - Restrictions (OpenIntuneBaseline macOS v1.0) sets none of these twelve ids, and no other template does. Siri is already off there (allowAssistant), so the ChatGPT integration via Siri was already largely closed; this policy also closes the integration in Writing Tools and signing in to an external service. Profile keys (com.apple.applicationaccess) and not DDM: in September 2026 Apple marks all twelve keys as deprecated from 26.4 onwards, in favour of the declarative configurations com.apple.configuration.intelligence.settings and com.apple.configuration.external-intelligence.settings (in Intune: intelligencesettings_* and externalintelligencesettings_*, which also exist for macOS). The profile keys nevertheless stay, and that has been worked through rather than postponed: those DDM configurations only exist from macOS 26.4 and Apple only allows them with supervised enrollment, whereas this payload also works on macOS 15 and on a Mac the user enrolled themselves. Converting now would leave Apple Intelligence unrestricted on 15.x and on 26.0 to 26.3, which is a regression. Deprecated does not mean removed at Apple either: the keys still work, and mSCP and OpenIntuneBaseline v2.0 beta use the same ones. Switch over once the fleet is on 26.4 or later and enrolled via ADE; then convert the whole policy and do not mix the two forms. The conversion is one-to-one: intelligencesettings_allowwritingtools, _allowgenmoji, _allowimageplayground, _allowappleintelligencereport and _forceondeviceonlydictation, the summaries under intelligencesettings_apps_mail, _apps_notes and _apps_safari, and externalintelligencesettings_enabled and _allowsignin. DDM can in addition do things this payload cannot (AllowImageWand, AllowVisualIntelligence, AllowPersonalizedHandwritingResults, ForceOnDeviceOnlyTranslation, Apps/Calendar), and that is a new choice, not part of the conversion. [Baseline] - IOS - D - Apple Intelligence Restricted is already declarative; there was no coverage of older versions to lose there. According to Apple, allowMailSummary only blocks manually summarising an email, not the automatic summaries. Anyone who does want to allow the ChatGPT integration, but only with the organisation's own business workspace, uses allowedExternalIntelligenceWorkspaceIDs — organisation-specific, so not included. Apple Intelligence only runs on Macs with Apple silicon and macOS 15.1 or later; on other Macs the settings do nothing. All are also valid on iOS/iPadOS; this policy is for macOS only. Deliberate deviation from OpenIntuneBaseline v2.0 beta: it leaves allowSafariSummary at true; false here, because a summarised web page may be an intranet or SharePoint page. The Apple Intelligence report (allowAppleIntelligenceReport) is off, as in OIB.

**Alternative to [Baseline] - MAC - D - Apple Intelligence Restricted.** That one sets the same twelve settings to the opposite value; assigning both results in a Conflict, after which Intune applies neither. forceOnDeviceOnlyDictation is false here: dictation may go through Apple's servers. Restricting the ChatGPT integration to the organisation's own business workspace is possible with allowedExternalIntelligenceWorkspaceIDs; organisation-specific, so not included. Siri stays off via [Baseline] - MAC - D - Restrictions (allowAssistant); anyone who wants the external integration via Siri must also reconsider that decision. That key has been deprecated since macOS 26.4 in favour of DDM sirisettings_enabled; why it stays is explained in the note on Restrictions.
teksten.**Alternatief van [Baseline] - WIN - D -: **Alternative to [Baseline] - WIN - D - Microsoft Edge DNS over HTTPS Secure** — both set `dnsoverhttpsmode` to a different value; assign one of them. Defender Network Protection (phase 1, Defender Antivirus) inspects Edge traffic via SmartScreen and therefore keeps working; for third-party browsers Network Protection relies on DNS/TLS inspection, and Microsoft advises turning off DoH and QUIC in that browser — that falls outside this Edge policy.

**Alternative to [Baseline] - WIN - D - Windows AI Features Restricted.** That policy sets the same four settings to the opposite value; assigning both results in a Conflict, after which Intune applies neither. Note that this only concerns the four Paint and Settings features: Recall and Click To Do are turned off separately via [Baseline] - WIN - D - Windows AI Restricted, and the Edge block list via [Baseline] - WIN - U - AI Usage Control Restricted. Anyone who wants to allow AI broadly must weigh those two as well.

**Alternative to [Baseline] - WIN - D - Windows AI Permitted.** That policy sets the same three settings to the opposite value; assigning both results in a Conflict, after which Intune applies neither. This is the variant the baseline deploys by default.

**Alternative to [Baseline] - WIN - D - Windows AI Restricted.** Before choosing this one, weigh whether the consequences are understood: Recall stores searchable screenshots on disk, and that index falls under the same retention periods and deletion obligations as the data it contains. In that case, also consider the Recall exclusion lists (setdenyapplistforrecall, setdenyurilistforrecall) and a retention period — these are deliberately not in this policy because they differ per organisation.
teksten.**Alternatief van [Baseline] - WIN - U -: **Alternative to [Baseline] - WIN - U - AI Usage Control Restricted.** A URL block list is friction rather than a boundary anyway: it does not work on a phone or on a personal device. Anyone who really wants to steer AI usage does so with the Generative AI category in Defender Web Content Filtering — that lives in the Defender portal, not in this repo.
teksten.**Bewust geen Permitted-tegenhanger** zo: **Deliberately no Permitted counterpart** as with Windows AI: for `assistcontentpolicy`, `_false` means "Intune changes nothing" and not "explicitly allowed", so a Permitted variant would not record a decision. Anyone who allows the assistants simply does not assign this policy. Microsoft 365 Copilot within the Microsoft apps is not covered here; it follows App Protection. teksten.**Bewuste afwijking van de bron:** Intun: **Deliberate deviation from the source:** IntuneAdmin sets 'Enumerate local users on domain-joined computers' to `_1` (Enabled), CIS L1 18.9.28.x requires Disabled; here `_0`. Three of these profiles (NTP server, Store upgrade offer, WinRT hosted content) may be L2 in the CIS benchmark itself; they are included because IntuneAdmin delivers them as L1 and they do not affect any workstation functionality. Overlap checked: `hideexclusionsfromlocaladmins` is in Defender Additional Configuration (different id), hiding connected users in Logon Hardening (different id). Hiding Defender exclusions from regular users (CIS) is deliberately not included here: OpenIntuneBaseline v4.0 dropped that setting because 'Hide Exclusions From Local Admins' in [Baseline] - WIN - D - Defender Additional Configuration already covers it.

**Deliberate deviation from the source:** IntuneAdmin sets PKU2U to `_1` (Allow), whereas CIS L1 2.3.11.3 requires 'Disabled'; here `_0` (Block). NetBT NodeType and LDAP signing require Windows 11 22H2 with the April 2025 update (10.0.22621.5126) or later; on older builds Intune reports 'Not applicable'. **Enforcing** Kerberos armoring (`requirekerberosarmoring`) is deliberately not included: that makes every sign-in fail against a domain that does not support armoring. SMB signing and NTLM audit are already in Local Security Policies and Security Hardening; WDigest and LLMNR in Legacy Hardening.
teksten.**Correctie september 2026.** De tekst z: **Correction September 2026.** Until now the text said that the organisation places no requirements on the personal side; the policy already required a device lock at the time (`passwordRequired`, `requiredPasswordComplexity: medium`). The requirement stays and the text has been corrected: it only requires that there is a lock of medium complexity, not which code, and the organisation does not see that code. Anyone who finds this unacceptable for personal devices must also reconsider the App Protection requirement on device complexity — otherwise App Protection blocks the apps anyway. Deliberately no `passwordExpirationDays` (NIST SP 800-63B advises against mandatory rotation) and no blocking of a shared lock for device and work profile (`blockUnifiedPasswordForWorkProfile`, UniFy W-11): two codes on a personal device mainly generates support requests, and the device code is already checked here. Fifteen minutes is aligned with iOS, macOS and Windows. The settings themselves are set by [Baseline] - AND - U - Work Profile Restrictions; this policy checks them.
teksten.**De app-lijst is bewust onvolledig.** W: **The app list is deliberately incomplete.** What it contains is what is defensible everywhere — an RDP session shows the screen of another system, a password vault shows passwords. Add the programs that display sensitive data in this environment: the HR package, the case management system, the banking environment. Names may be an executable (`app.exe`) or an AUMID for Store apps. Note that the 30-day retention period says nothing about deletion obligations: if a piece of personal data is in the index, that index falls under the same rules as the source. Export is already off by default; it is set explicitly here so that it is a decision and not a coincidence.

teksten.ALLEEN voor gedeelde apparaten. Windows: ONLY for shared devices. By default, Windows turns a network that a user adds themselves into an all-user profile: every other user of that device sees that SSID in the list and can connect to it. Reading the password only works as a local administrator, and in this baseline that is limited to the LAPS account (wlapsadmin by default) — but the SSID list itself already reveals where a colleague has been. Per-user profiles do exist in Windows (netsh wlan add profile user=current), but the interface never creates them that way and there is no MDM or Settings Catalog setting that enforces it: the corresponding GPO sits in Wireless Network (IEEE 802.11) Policies and is domain-bound. What is possible is the other way round: only allow networks from Intune. TWO PREREQUISITES. First deploy a Wi-Fi profile via Intune, otherwise the device is offline once this is applied. And never put this policy on laptops: home and hotel networks will then no longer work, and teleworking should simply be possible. Microsoft also warns that existing user-created profiles are removed when it is applied — that is the intent here, but announce it in advance.
teksten.Alleen voor organisaties die NinjaOne of: Only for organisations that use NinjaOne or TeamViewer. Fixes the privacy permissions (PPPC) of the management tools: NinjaOne Remote and TeamViewer get Accessibility so that remote control works, and the three NinjaOne components get Full Disk Access — without the user having to approve it, and without them being able to revoke it.

Only for organisations that use NinjaOne or TeamViewer. teksten.Als `androidWorkProfileCompliancePolicy`: Written as `androidWorkProfileCompliancePolicy` — the personal work profile. `hardwareBacked` excludes older devices without supported hardware attestation — that is intended, but check it against the fleet before you assign. Since September 2026 this policy also requires a security patch of 2026-03-01 or later (six months back, the same as the warning in App Protection); devices from manufacturers that patch quarterly stay well within it. The OS minimum (12.0) and the patch date go stale: run `node scripts/check-osversion.js` to see how far behind they are. Both are currency targets (see `ondergrens`) and may move along, but not without checking how many devices fall below them. Defender for Endpoint is deliberately in a separate policy (Compliance Defender for Endpoint), because it requires a licence and connector.

teksten.Bewust **niet** opgenomen: allowpassword: Deliberately **not** included: allowpasswordautofill=false (UniFy Corporate) — that also disables passkeys and password managers; forceauthenticationbeforeautofill is used instead. iCloud backup and iCloud Drive off (UniFy Corporate) — an organisational decision about where data may be stored, not hardening; managed apps already do not sync to iCloud via [Baseline] - IOS - D - Data Protection. Blocking Bluetooth, NFC, hotspot and VPN changes (Connectivity Controls, L2) — breaks car kits, payment cards and working from home. Siri fully off — only Siri on the lock screen is off. Host pairing (Finder/iTunes) is handled by the enrollment profile (iTunesPairingMode disallow), not by this policy. allowopenfromunmanagedtomanaged not blocked: otherwise a photo from the Photos app can no longer be shared in Outlook or Teams — the same trade-off as with allowedInboundDataTransferSources in App Protection. Control Center off on the lock screen also means: no flashlight without unlocking. Corrections to UniFy: forceautomaticdateandtime is false there (= not enforced), true here. Activation Lock: UniFy blocks it (false); allowed here (true), because a supervised device then has theft protection while Intune keeps the bypass code (device action 'Disable Activation Lock'). Before rollout, check that Intune shows a bypass code for a test device; without that code a returned device with a personal Apple Account cannot be reused — in that case choose false. This policy shares the top-level group com.apple.applicationaccess with Data Protection but does not set any key twice; iOS merges restriction payloads.
teksten.Bewust `usbdataaccess_disallowusbfiletra: Deliberately `usbdataaccess_disallowusbfiletransfer` and not `disallowusbdatatransfer` (UniFy): the latter blocks all USB data, including wired headsets, docks and Android Auto. Not adopted from the UniFy corporate set: `airplanemodeblocked` (airplane mode impossible), `minimumwifisecuritylevel_personalnetworksecurity` (open and guest networks such as in hotels and trains stop working), `cellularblockwifitethering`, `wifidirectsettings_disallowed`, `ultrawidebandblocked`, `vpnconfigblocked`, `mobilenetworksconfigblocked`, `networkresetblocked` and `cellbroadcastsconfigblocked` (break working from home or travelling, or bring no security gain), `accountsblockmodification` and `certificatecredentialconfigurationdisabled` (first require automatic account provisioning and a SCEP/PKCS profile, UniFy W-5/W-6), `locationmode_enforced` (location always on is a privacy decision), `securitycommoncriteriamodeenabled` (Samsung only, W-25), `passwordexpirationdays` (NIST SP 800-63B), `bluetoothblockcontactsharing` (no more caller name in the car) and `passwordblockkeyguard_true` (that is *Disable lock screen* — an error in UniFy FM). Also not: `appsallowinstallfromunknownsources_false` and `securitydevelopersettingsenabled_false` — for these Android settings `_false` means "not configured", and on device owner devices both are already closed by default. The screen timeout (`screentimeout`, 900 seconds) limits how long the screen stays on; the lock time itself is checked by Compliance Corporate Password. 2G blocking: in regions with only 2G coverage there is no longer any mobile reception; emergency calls keep working. App updates set to `always` also run over mobile data; anyone who wants to test line-of-business apps first chooses `wifionly` or their own update policy (UniFy W-9).
teksten.Bewust één policy met Medium in plaats v: Deliberately one policy with Medium instead of UniFy's Low for corporate devices: Low makes a device non-compliant at even a low risk, and that first requires experience with how often that happens. A separate policy alongside Compliance Device Health, so that a tenant without an MDE licence can keep using Device Health as is; compliance policies are evaluated independently and do not conflict. Block action after 24 hours, same as the other iOS compliance policies. The field advancedThreatProtectionRequiredSecurityLevel is not in pl4nty DCv1 for iOS but is in Graph beta iosCompliancePolicy and in both source exports. Onboarding: [Baseline] - IOS - D - Defender for Endpoint Onboarding Supervised and … Unsupervised; app configuration in IntuneTemplate/IOS/AppConfiguration.
teksten.Bewust géén `passcodeExpirationDays`: he: Deliberately no `passcodeExpirationDays`: forcing periodic changes of a device passcode demonstrably leads to weaker passcodes, and NIST SP 800-63B explicitly advises against mandatory rotation without cause. Fifteen minutes is aligned with the macOS and Windows compliance policies in the baseline.
teksten.Bewust géén `passwordExpirationDays` (Un: Deliberately no `passwordExpirationDays` (UniFy: 365): NIST SP 800-63B advises against mandatory rotation. Fifteen minutes instead of UniFy's five, the same as iOS, macOS, Windows and the work profile; CIS specifies ≤ 2 minutes, and UniFy also deliberately deviates from that. The settings themselves are set by [Baseline] - AND - U - Corporate Device Security; without that policy the user is not prompted to choose a code that meets these requirements.
teksten.Bewust geen toestelcode: op een kiosk me: Deliberately no device code: a single-app kiosk often has none, and on a shared device Managed Home Screen handles the session PIN. Deliberately no OS minimum: rugged devices (scanners, tills) stay on an older major version for a long time but still receive patches from the manufacturer — the patch date (2026-03-01) is the honest measure there. Before assigning, check whether the fleet passes hardware attestation; old kiosk hardware sometimes fails it immediately (UniFy W-18). In addition, devices in Entra shared device mode do not receive the user policies of whoever is signed in — on dedicated devices Intune applies only device assignments.
teksten.Bewust níet overgenomen uit UniFy: `work: Deliberately not adopted from UniFy: `workProfilePasswordExpirationDays` (365 — NIST SP 800-63B advises against rotation), `workProfileBlockCrossProfileCallerId` and `workProfileBlockCrossProfileContactsSearch` (break the name display for an incoming work call in the personal phone app), `workProfileBlockAddingAccounts` and `workProfileAccountUse: blockAll` (can cause adding the work account in apps to fail, UniFy W-6), `workProfileBlockPersonalAppInstallsFromUnknownSources` (a requirement on the personal side; Compliance Device Health already checks unknown sources), `workProfileBlockNotificationsWhileDeviceLocked` (App Protection already hides organisation data in notifications) and `blockUnifiedPasswordForWorkProfile` (see Compliance Password). `requiredPasswordComplexity: medium` at device level is a requirement on the personal side, but the same one that Compliance Password and App Protection already impose — without this line the user is not prompted to set it and simply becomes non-compliant. Two fields (`requiredPasswordComplexity`, `workProfileRequiredPasswordComplexity`) are not in the pl4nty definitions but are in UniFy's Graph export; on Android 12+ they are the ones that apply, length and type only on older versions.
teksten.Bewust zonder toewijzing: hoort op een g: Deliberately unassigned: belongs on a group of shared devices. Not an Endpoint Security template but a regular Settings Catalog policy, because DisablePostLogonProvisioning is not in the Account Protection template. The four overlapping settings have the same value as in the device policy, so side by side on the same device they do not cause a conflict — this policy only adds DisablePostLogonProvisioning.
teksten.Bewuste afwijking van OpenIntuneBaseline: Deliberate deviation from OpenIntuneBaseline v2.0 beta: it sets askForPasswordDelay to 60 seconds, this policy to 5, the CIS value. Sixty seconds means that someone who walks away just as the screen saver starts leaves an open Mac behind for a minute; with Touch ID, unlocking immediately costs the user almost nothing. OIB's moduleName (Flurry) is omitted: cosmetic. Relationship with [Baseline] - MAC - D - Passcode and Screen Lock: there maxInactivity is set to 15 minutes (com.apple.mobiledevice.passwordpolicy), which macOS translates into a maximum for the screen saver. Here idleTime (com.apple.screensaver.user) and loginWindowIdleTime (com.apple.screensaver) are set to 900 seconds: the same 15 minutes, different settingDefinitionIds, so no Intune conflict and no contradictory value. maxGracePeriod is not set in that policy; askForPasswordDelay here is therefore the only grace period. com.apple.screensaver.user is a payload of its own in the settings catalog; microsoft/intune-my-macs (pol-sec-005) delivers it in the same form at device level. Check in the pilot with `sudo profiles show -type configuration` that idleTime arrives; if it does not, maxInactivity already covers the 15 minutes.

teksten.De agressiviteit staat op Low: alleen bl: The aggressiveness is set to Low: only block when Defender is 100 percent certain. That is the value with the smallest chance of a false positive, and a false positive is expensive here — you then block a legitimate process that updates files on a share, for example a backup or a sync tool. Medium and High block from 99 and 90 percent certainty respectively; only consider those once reporting shows that nothing legitimate is hit. IntuneAdmin ships this setting on Audit; here it is Block, because detecting without blocking does not stop encryption.
teksten.De baseline zet telemetrie bewust op Opt: The baseline deliberately sets telemetry to Optional because Endpoint Analytics and Windows Update reporting rely on it. That is a defensible choice, but it is at odds with data minimisation under the GDPR. These two settings take the sharp edge off without breaking the reporting: the level stays, but additional diagnostic log files and memory dumps — which may contain user data — are not sent. That is the answer to the question a DPO or auditor asks here.

teksten.De lichtste van de drie varianten: één i: The lightest of the three variants: one setting, no position on shared folders. Applies only to classic Outlook (the Win32 app from Microsoft 365 Apps); the new Outlook for Windows does not read these ADMX settings and has no OST. The well-known slider **amount of mail to keep offline** (3 months / 12 months / all, registry value `SyncWindowSetting`) is *not* in the settings catalog: the ingested `outlk16v2` ADMX has eighteen settings under *Cached Exchange Mode* and that slider is not one of them. teksten.De macOS-tegenhanger van BitLocker; hers: The macOS counterpart of BitLocker; the recovery key is stored in Intune. Since September 2026 the personal recovery key is explicitly created (userecoverykey) and not shown to the user (showrecoverykey), so it can only be retrieved via Intune.
teksten.De macrobeveiliging van Office: blokkeer: Office macro security: blocks macros in files from the internet, restricts ActiveX and old file formats. The centrepiece of this baseline against phishing via attachments.
teksten.De naam zegt waar hij over gaat: dit is: The name says what it is about: this is the PIN of the WHfB passkey, not that of a FIDO2 security key — that one lives on the key itself. teksten.De opdracht noemde een aparte 'Data Prot: The assignment called for a separate 'Data Protection BYOD'. It has become a single policy: the same keys with the same values in both a BYOD and a Corporate variant would mean double maintenance, and [Baseline] - IOS - D - Restrictions Corporate contains only what requires supervision. Contacts: allowunmanagedtoreadmanagedcontacts=false (personal apps cannot read work contacts, the same as the Apple default but explicit), but allowmanagedtowriteunmanagedcontacts=**true** — with open-in separation enabled, Outlook otherwise cannot write contacts to the Contacts app and the user sees no name on an incoming call; the same reason why contactSyncBlocked in App Protection is deliberately off. allowopenfromunmanagedtomanaged and requiremanagedpasteboard deliberately not: photos from the personal library remain shareable with work apps (see ANALYSE.md). Not adopted from UniFy BYOD: allowscreenshot=false (screenshots off on the entire personal device; App Protection already blocks them within the managed apps), allowcloudprivaterelay=false and forceairplayoutgoingrequestspairingpassword (privacy/convenience, not data separation).

teksten.Declaratieve variant (DDM) in plaats van:
Declarative variant (DDM) instead of the com.apple.softwareupdate settings that OpenIntuneBaseline v1.0 provides. The three automatic actions are set to AlwaysOn (`_1`); until September 2026 they were set to `_0` (Allowed), and then nothing was enforced.

**Enforce Latest (September 2026).** Delay in Days 30, Install Time 12:30. Microsoft: the delay counts from the release date of the update (or the creation of the policy) and 'only determines the target enforcement date and not the date that the update is offered to users'. 30 is deliberately larger than any deferral above (7/14/21): with OIB's 3 days the deadline would fall before a major update becomes visible through the 14-day deferral. 30 days is also the CIS limit (1.1, 1.6) and the maximum of the setting. 12:30 because a Mac is on during the day; at night it sleeps and only installs when opened. Enforce Latest enforces the newest version for that model, **including a new major version**: macOS 27 becomes visible 14 days after release and is enforced after 30 days. If an organisation wants to release major versions themselves, remove this group and use a policy with a target version. Microsoft Learn: 'When an update enforcement is assigned, the device ignores software update settings, including automatic update actions' — as long as a deadline is open, it determines the behaviour; the automatic actions apply outside of that.

**Beta** (softwareupdate_beta ProgramEnrollment AlwaysOff): no AppleSeed/beta builds on corporate Macs; macOS 15.4+, supervised.

**App updates and configuration data** via two keys from the classic com.apple.SoftwareUpdate payload (AutomaticallyInstallAppUpdates, ConfigDataInstall), because the DDM declaration has no counterpart for them — mSCP (branch tahoe) also maps exactly these two CIS rules only to the profile keys. Both are already on by default in macOS; the policy makes them no longer switchable off. The other keys from that payload are deliberately not set, because DDM covers them.

Open point: whether SystemPeriodInDays (21) also delays XProtect and configuration data is not defined in Apple's schema. If it turns out to do so, lower it.

teksten.Drempel 10 en niet 5: bij 5 tikt een geb: Threshold 10 and not 5: at 5 a user who makes a mistake locks themselves out too easily, and 10 is the value of the Microsoft Security Baseline. The machine threshold (InteractiveLogon MachineAccountLockoutThreshold) does something else: it puts the device into BitLocker recovery after ten failed attempts, and then the recovery key is needed. teksten.Eén van drie varianten op dezelfde as —: One of three variants on the same axis — assign one, never two: this one, Cached Mode Default (cached mode on only) or Cached Mode Off (Online mode). The user's own mailbox is cached, so Outlook works offline and searching is local. What is attached to it is not: a shared mailbox added to the profile is the main cause of OST files of tens of gigabytes, and reading it online is no practical loss. Note the polarity of the two shared folder settings, which run opposite to each other: *Disable shared mail folder caching* set to **Enabled** writes `cacheothersmail=0`, and *Download shared non-mail folders* set to **Disabled** writes `downloadsharedfolders=0`. Both zeros mean do not cache. Applies only to classic Outlook (the Win32 app from Microsoft 365 Apps); the new Outlook for Windows does not read these ADMX settings and has no OST. Belongs with [Baseline] - MAC - D - Platform SSO and does nothing without that policy: the cloud TGT is issued by Platform SSO; this profile only tells Apple's Kerberos extension which realm goes with it and that it may use that TGT (`usePlatformSSOTGT`). `performKerberosOnly` keeps the extension away from password expiry checks, password synchronisation and the home directory path — those belong to Platform SSO, not here.

A second policy alongside Platform SSO and not an extension of it: the settings catalog has two separate forms for `com.apple.extensiblesso`, the Platform SSO form (`com.apple.extensiblesso_com.apple.extensiblesso`) and the Kerberos form this policy uses (`com.apple.extensiblesso_com.apple.extensiblesso-kerberos_kerberos`). Each Kerberos realm is one such form, with its own `Realm` and its own `Hosts`. On the Mac those profiles are installed side by side and macOS merges the payloads; check-scope.js therefore deliberately does not report that overlap on Apple as a conflict.

The tenant id is in the `preferredKDCs` URL as `%OrganizationId%`, the same construction as in the OneDrive KFM and Teams policies: CIPP replaces that token at deployment with the tenant's customerId (see Get-CIPPTextReplacement in CIPP-API); `%tenantid%` does the same. If you deploy with IntuneBackupAndRestore instead of CIPP, that replacement does not happen and you have to fill in the id by hand.

On the tenant side, four things must be in place before this profile achieves anything: Entra Kerberos enabled on the storage account, admin consent on the associated service principal, MFA off for that storage account's Entra app, and share-level permissions on the share itself. If the file share already exists, the identifier URI of that app registration is `CIFS/<account>.file.core.windows.net` — in capitals. macOS only mounts on `cifs/` in lower case; Microsoft provides `updateappmanifestazurefiles.ps1` for this in azure-files-samples. New shares do not have that problem.

**A storage account that already has another identity source is ruled out.** If the account uses Microsoft Entra Domain Services then Entra Kerberos and AD DS are greyed out in the portal with "Another access method is already configured". A storage account can only have one. On a Mac with a valid cloud TGT, `kgetcred cifs/<account>.file.core.windows.net@KERBEROS.MICROSOFTONLINE.COM` then returns AADSTS700016 — there is no app registration for the file service, so there is nothing to issue. Entra DS is not an alternative route to the same goal either: Platform SSO only issues `tgt_cloud` (Entra Kerberos) and `tgt_ad` (on-premises AD via Cloud Kerberos Trust), and Entra DS is neither. Changing the identity source affects all existing traffic to those shares, including the file- and folder-level permissions set with Entra DS identities; see "Change the identity source for Azure file shares" at Microsoft. The full diagnosis is in IntuneTemplate/MAC/PlatformScripts/README.md.

**What is needed to deploy this.** A storage account with Entra Kerberos as its identity source. If the existing account uses something else and cannot be switched, a **second storage account** is needed with Entra Kerberos as its identity source — the two can coexist; the restriction applies per account, not per tenant. This profile does not need to change for that: `Hosts` covers every storage account with `.windows.net`, and only the mount script in `IntuneTemplate/MAC/PlatformScripts/` names an account. If that is not worth the effort, the honest conclusion is that SMB is the wrong vehicle here and the data belongs in SharePoint, with `automountteamsites` from the settings catalog — that works on both platforms without Kerberos and without VPN.

The on-premises AD side would be a second policy of this form, with its own realm and its own domain name in `Hosts`. It is not included here — this baseline assumes cloud-only devices. If it is added, the on-prem profile should be deployed first and this one after it, in that order. The TGT mapping itself can be controlled with `custom_tgt_setting` in the extension data of the Platform SSO policy (Company Portal 2508+); the default value 0 maps both the on-prem and the cloud TGT, which is why that policy does not need to change for this profile.

For Platform SSO profiles Microsoft says "assign to users, not to devices". This baseline keeps macOS profiles on device groups, same as the existing Platform SSO policy. As long as the policy is in phase 3 this makes no practical difference: it is created and not assigned.

Verify after deployment: `app-sso platform -s` in Terminal must show a ticket with `ticketKeyPath` = `tgt_cloud`, and `nc -vz <account>.file.core.windows.net 445` must be open. That the Kerberos extension's menu bar extra reports "Not signed in" is normal and does not mean it is not working.

teksten.Keuze voor de klassieke payload en niet: Choice of the classic payload and not the declarative passcode configuration (passcode_*). Both apply to iOS and neither requires supervision, but two sources contradict each other on 'no simple code'. The Intune catalog says for RequireComplexPasscode that the code must also contain a character other than digits and letters, which makes a six-digit numeric code impossible; Apple's own schema only says that the code may not contain repeated or ascending or descending characters (such as 123 or CBA), exactly what allowSimple=false did, and places the requirement for a special character under a different key: MinimumComplexCharacters. Which of the two describes the behaviour has not been tested here, so the classic payload stays. It is, however, an open question and not an end point, because Microsoft lists the classic Passcode payload as deprecated since Apple OS 27. The payload here is the same as in [Baseline] - MAC - D - Passcode and Screen Lock and in both UniFy sets. Five minutes of inactivity is stricter than the fifteen minutes that Compliance Password checks; a device with this policy is therefore always compliant. Deliberately no maxpinageindays (NIST SP 800-63B: no rotation without cause) and no pinhistory. UniFy Corporate sets 1 minute and 5 attempts; a wipe after five attempts conflicts with the norm rule of this baseline.
teksten.Organisatiekeuze. Pariteit met [Baseline: Organisational decision. teksten.MAM voor persoonlijke iPhones/iPads: bed: MAM for personal iPhones/iPads: corporate data in the Microsoft apps gets a PIN, encryption and copy restrictions, without the device itself being managed. Since September 2026 this policy also warns on iOS below 18.0. Deliberately the **warning** variant and not `minimumRequired*`: the latter blocks the app, and that should be a separate decision, taken after you have seen in the reporting how many devices it affects. That value goes stale — run `node scripts/check-osversion.js` to see how far behind it is. It is in `veldOverrides` because OIB leaves it empty; without that entry the next `import-oib.js` silently reverts it. Since September 2026 also allowWidgetContentSync=false: widgets of managed apps show no organisation data, in line with notifications without organisation data. Deliberately not the iOS 26 fields writingToolsConfigurationState and genmojiConfigurationState: whether to allow Apple Intelligence is an organisational decision (see [Baseline] - IOS - D - Apple Intelligence Restricted/Permitted for enrolled devices), and this policy is one for everyone. Also not blockDataIngestionIntoOrganizationDocuments=true (UniFy L2): with only OneDrive, SharePoint and camera as sources, a user can no longer put a photo from their library into a work document — the same trade-off as with allowedInboundDataTransferSources.

teksten.maxInactivity kan in de settings catalog: maxInactivity cannot be set higher than 15 minutes in the settings catalog — which happens to be exactly the value the compliance policy requires. maxFailedAttempts is deliberately omitted: on macOS it leads to an increasing wait time and eventually a lockout that can only be opened with the FileVault recovery key, and that is a separate trade-off. This policy sets no com.apple.applicationaccess or com.apple.screensaver setting and therefore does not clash with MAC - D - Restrictions. Since Apple OS 27, Microsoft lists the classic Passcode payload as deprecated, with the declarative passcode configuration (passcode_*, macOS 13 and later) as its successor. Whether RequireComplexPasscode there means the same as no simple passcode is uncertain, because the Intune catalog and Apple's schema contradict each other; the trade-off is described at [Baseline] - IOS - D - Passcode. Note: users with a shorter or simpler password must change it at their next sign-in. Since September 2026 [Baseline] - MAC - D - Screensaver sets the com.apple.screensaver keys: ask for the password 5 seconds after the screen saver starts and start the screen saver after 900 seconds, also in the login window. Those are the same 15 minutes as maxInactivity here, with different settingDefinitionIds — no conflict, and only together do they make a Mac that really asks for a password after 15 minutes.

teksten.OIB dekt alleen de OS-schijf. De 11 eige: OIB only covers the OS disk. teksten.OIB dekt verwisselbare media niet. Allee: OIB does not cover removable media. Only writing is blocked, not reading: data may come in, not go out. The BitLocker policy deliberately leaves removabledrivesrequireencryption off — with a write block, an encryption requirement adds nothing.
teksten.OIB noemt deze policy U omdat zij 'm aan: OIB calls this policy U because it assigns it to users; all 12 settings are device-scoped, so here it is D (see check-scope.js). Since OIB v4.0 this also contains the lock after 15 minutes of inactivity (interactivelogon_machineinactivitylimit_v2 = 900): the replacement for the discontinued Password compliance policy, and a setting the baseline previously set in Local Security Policies. Sleep on AC power goes to 30 minutes along with it, so that locking and sleeping do not happen at the same moment.
teksten.OIB wijst deze aan gebruikers toe om een: OIB assigns this to users to avoid a restart in the middle of Autopilot; all 8 settings are device-scoped, hence D here. Keep in mind that the first application requires a restart.
teksten.OIB's policy is gemengd (4 user- en 1 de: OIB's policy is mixed (4 user settings and 1 device setting at top level). Split because a mixed policy cannot be assigned unambiguously.

teksten.Rotatie op 6 maanden (optie _5), gelijk: Rotation every 6 months (option _5), same as the rotation of the FileVault recovery key in [Baseline] - MAC - D - FileVault; intune-my-macs rotates monthly, which mainly generates service desk traffic without lowering the risk — the password is only used by whoever requests it. Viewing the password: Devices → device → Passwords and keys → Recovery Lock Password. That requires the Intune permissions 'Remote tasks/View macOS recovery lock password' (and for rotation 'Rotate macOS recovery lock password'); limit who has them, preferably via PIM. After use: device action 'Rotate recovery lock passcode'. Unenrolling from Intune wipes the password from the Mac; removing the assignment makes Intune attempt to wipe it. So a Mac that leaves the organisation should first be unenrolled, then released in Apple Business (see IntuneTemplate/MAC/Enrollment/apple-business).
teksten.Roteert automatisch het wachtwoord van h: Automatically rotates the password of the local administrator account and stores it in Entra ID, so that no shared administrator password circulates any more.
teksten.Ruimt automatisch tijdelijke bestanden,: Automatically cleans up temporary files, the Recycle Bin and old downloads as soon as the disk threatens to fill up, and makes locally cached OneDrive files online-only again.
teksten.Scheiding tussen wie policies wijzigt, w: Separation between who changes policies, who approves them (PR review) and who grants exceptions; set up Entra/Intune RBAC and PIM — outside the scope of this baseline.

Full Disk Access for OneDrive is not here either: [Baseline] - MAC - D - Microsoft OneDrive already does that.
teksten.Schermvergrendeling, wachtwoord- en PIN-: Screen lock, password and PIN requirements, managed local administrators, LAPS, removable storage, enrolment and compliance as an access condition.

teksten.Schrijven naar USB-sticks, externe schij: Writing to USB sticks, external drives and phones is blocked, and a user notices that immediately. teksten.Scriptblok-logging stond al aan in [Base: Script block logging was already on in [Baseline] - WIN - D - Security Hardening; it has been deliberately left out here to avoid a conflict. What was missing is transcription: script block logging shows which code was loaded, the transcript shows the session itself with input, output and timestamps. Logging policy usually asks for the latter. One caveat: transcripts end up in the user's profile by default, where that same user can delete them. If logs must stay out of the user's reach, fill outputdirectory with a central share as soon as there is one.

teksten.Sinds OIB v4.0 één toets per policy in p: Since OIB v4.0 one check per policy instead of four bundled policies, so that grace periods and exceptions can be handled per check. teksten.Sinds OIB v4.0 is dit de voormalige 24H2: Since OIB v4.0 this is the former 24H2+ variant: the base variant has been dropped because Windows 11 23H2 stops receiving updates on 10 November 2026. In content that variant differs on one point: the built-in Administrator account is disabled (enableadministratoraccountstatus). teksten.SSID en PSK staan op `<SSID-CORPORATE>`: SSID and PSK are set to `<SSID-CORPORATE>` and `<PSK-CORPORATE>`. Fill them in before you assign; with the placeholder in place, the profile connects on no device at all. The password ends up in this template and therefore in this repo. There is no CIPP token for a PSK the way %OrganizationId% exists for the tenant id, and leaving a placeholder does not work here: Graph never returns a PSK — a tenant backup only includes `preSharedKeyIsSet: true`. So if you fill it in in the tenant instead of here, the next CIPP sync writes the placeholder over it again and every device loses its Wi-Fi. Fill it in here, and only as long as this repo is private; if it is ever shared, rotate the PSK. That the PSK remains a shared secret regardless is already covered in the notes for [Baseline] - WIN - D - Wireless and Peripherals: a local administrator simply reads it with `netsh wlan show profile key=clear`, and the measure that does solve this is 802.1X with certificates. `connectToPreferredNetwork` is deliberately false here and true in Wifi Guest: this is the preferred network, so Windows does not need to look elsewhere. Note the interplay with [Baseline] - WIN - D - Wireless Shared Devices: that policy only allows networks deployed by Intune and therefore needs this profile to avoid taking a shared device offline. This is the policy that is the prerequisite for it.

teksten.Vraagt een herstart, en geheugenintegrit: Requires a restart, and memory integrity (HVCI) does not load drivers that were not built for it — think of old VPN, printer and dock drivers. Check in the pilot that everything still starts.

teksten.Wacht op de eerste iOS-inschrijving. Een: Awaiting the first iOS enrolment. A compliance policy only affects an enrolled device; as long as iOS runs only via App Protection without enrolment, it does nothing.
teksten.Wacht op de eerste iOS-inschrijving. Geb: Awaiting the first iOS enrolment. Users will notice that 'Open in' from managed apps no longer offers personal apps.
teksten.Wacht op de eerste iOS-inschrijving. Let: Awaiting the first iOS enrolment. Watch out during the first deployment: a user with a four-digit or simple passcode must change it at the next unlock.
teksten.Wacht op de eerste iOS-inschrijving. Na: Awaiting the first iOS enrolment. After the deadline the device installs the update itself at 02:00 and restarts — announce this and watch how it lands on the first devices.
teksten.Wacht op de Microsoft Defender for Endpo: Awaiting the Microsoft Defender for Endpoint connector in Intune (Endpoint security → Microsoft Defender for Endpoint → 'Connect Windows devices … to Defender for Endpoint' on) and a Defender for Endpoint P1/P2 or Business licence. Without the connector, every device reports 'not compliant' or 'not available' on this check.
teksten.Wacht op drie voorwaarden: een Defender: Awaiting three prerequisites: a Defender for Endpoint licence for the user, the Intune connector for Defender for Endpoint with iOS/iPadOS enabled, and the Defender app on the device. Only assign it once those are in place — otherwise a device without a risk signal may, depending on the connector setting, come out as non-compliant.

Awaiting three prerequisites: a Defender for Endpoint licence, the Defender–Intune connector with Android enabled, and the Defender app deployed via Managed Google Play. Without those three, every device becomes non-compliant.
teksten.Wacht op een fully managed- of corporate: Awaiting a fully managed or corporate-owned work profile enrolment, and a Defender for Endpoint licence, the connector with Android enabled and the Defender app via Managed Google Play.
teksten.Wacht tot er een storage account met Ent: Waits until there is a storage account with Entra Kerberos as identity source. An account that is already on Microsoft Entra Domain Services or AD DS cannot have that at the same time, and switching it affects everything already running on that account. On a Mac with a valid cloud TGT, such an account yields AADSTS700016 — the KDC knows no application for that file service. The profile itself is finished and account-independent: `Hosts` is set to `.windows.net` and thus covers every storage account. As soon as there is one with Entra Kerberos this can move to phase 1, with as second prerequisite that Microsoft enables the tenant for the macOS preview (azurefiles@microsoft.com).
teksten.Wat er van de oude Administrative Templa: What remains of the old Administrative Templates policy (008) after OIB took over the rest: hardened UNC paths, WDigest, blocking of device classes, multicast DNS, LSA custom SSP/AP, MPR notifications, standby behaviour and Group Policy registry processing. Kept separate so that an OIB upgrade does not silently drag these settings along or throw them away.
Refuses all NTLM, inbound and outbound. Whatever cannot use Kerberos breaks: applications that connect by IP address, devices outside the domain, and shares for which the device gets no Kerberos ticket — an Entra-joined device opening a share on Entra Domain Services falls back to NTLM. Before the pilot, read Microsoft-Windows-NTLM/Operational on a few Windows 11 24H2 devices (4020/4021 outbound, 4022/4023 inbound): that logging is enabled there by default and shows what would break.
teksten.Werken op Windows Pro. Alleen Credential: Work on Windows Pro. Only Credential Guard within that same policy requires Enterprise.
teksten.Werkt via de TenantLockdown-CSP en geldt: Works via the TenantLockdown CSP and applies from the next clean installation. Make sure wired or Wi-Fi is available during OOBE — with a fleet without Ethernet and without a pre-configured Wi-Fi profile, the user gets stuck.
teksten.Wie de Windows-lijn wil — lezen mag, sch: Anyone who wants the Windows approach — reading allowed, writing not — needs Microsoft Defender for Endpoint Device Control on macOS (a removable media policy with read-only rights). That requires an onboarded Defender agent (IntuneTemplate/MAC/EndpointSecurity) and a separate JSON policy, and is not part of this round. An external Time Machine disk is also no longer mounted with this policy; in this baseline, backup is meant to go through OneDrive (KFM). If an organisation chooses this, deploy to a pilot group first and then treat it as phase 2. No overlap: no other template sets diskmanagement_*.
teksten.Wie gewend is het scherm binnen een minu: Anyone used to getting the screen back without a password within a minute of the screen saver must now use their password or Touch ID straight away. Noticeable, not breaking; pilot and announce first.
teksten.Wie recoveryOS nodig heeft — macOS opnie: Anyone who needs recoveryOS — reinstalling macOS, Disk Utility from recovery, another startup disk — must from now on request the password from the service desk. Check in the pilot that the password is visible in Intune before you deploy broadly.
teksten.Wijzigingen bij Microsoft/leveranciers v: Track changes at Microsoft/suppliers (Message Center, roadmaps) and review them periodically.
teksten.Wijzigingsbeheer voor de baseline (PR-re: Change management for the baseline (PR review, pilot)
teksten.Wijzigingsprocedure (PR-review, pilotfas: Define and follow a change procedure (PR review, pilot phase, communication); update rings are the technical side.
teksten.Windows 11 24H2 en hoger; op oudere buil: Windows 11 24H2 and later; on older builds the setting does nothing.
teksten.Windows Connect Now is de vergeten route: Windows Connect Now is the forgotten route: with it, a user can transfer wireless settings — including the network password — via WPS or a USB stick from one device to another, outside any management. Both settings close that off. On the question of who can see each other's Wi-Fi profiles: profiles deployed via Intune or GPO are device-wide and therefore visible to every user of that device, and anyone who adds a network themselves can retrieve the associated password in plain text with netsh. As long as the corporate network runs on a shared password (PSK), every user who has ever connected therefore knows that password — no policy helps against that. The measure that does solve this is 802.1X with certificates, because then there is no shared secret to read out. Blocking manual Wi-Fi configuration altogether (AllowManualWiFiConfiguration) is deliberately left out: that makes working from home and hotels impossible, and teleworking should simply be possible. Stricter policies sometimes require all Bluetooth profiles except Serial Port Profile to be turned off. Implementing that literally breaks headphones, mice and keyboards; that first requires a decision. These four settings are the defensible intermediate step: the device can no longer be discovered or approached by a stranger, and existing pairings keep working. ServicesAllowedList is deliberately left out — it requires GUIDs per profile and, without a carefully compiled list, turns off more than intended.
teksten.Windows Hello for Business per gebruiker: Windows Hello for Business per user instead of per device: the same requirements as the device policy — TPM required, PIN of at least six characters, PIN recovery on — but bound to the user. Intended for users with their own device; shared devices should be excluded here with a device filter.
teksten.Windows Hello for Business voor gedeelde: Windows Hello for Business for shared devices that several users sign in to. Same requirements as the regular device policy, but without setup immediately after sign-in: on a shared device every user would otherwise be guided through PIN setup at their first sign-in.
teksten.Windows Protected Print laat printers va: Windows Protected Print drops printers that have no Mopria driver. Inventory the printer fleet first.
teksten.Windows Protected Print vraagt Windows 1: Windows Protected Print requires Windows 11 24H2 or later and drops printers that do not have a Mopria driver — in practice those are older network printers and label printers. Inventory the printer fleet before you assign this broadly; on a fleet without its own printers it is free. The other two settings are unconditionally safe. Overlap checked (September 2026): `printers_configurewindowsprotectedprint` is only in this policy; [Baseline] - WIN - D - Printing sets twenty other printer ids (Point and Print, RPC, RedirectionGuard, driver installation by administrators only) and does not clash. ANALYSE.md still lists Protected Print as 'deliberately not adopted' — that is no longer correct: it is here, in phase 2.
teksten.Zet alleen Cached Exchange Mode aan en l: Only turns on Cached Exchange Mode and leaves the rest at Outlook's default — so shared folders are cached too.
teksten.Zet Apple Intelligence-functies uit die: Turns off Apple Intelligence features that have text, email, notes, web pages or images processed by a language model or sent to an external AI service, and keeps dictation on the device.
teksten.Zet bewust geen minimumlengte: die staat: Deliberately sets no minimum length: that is already set to 6 in WIN - D - Windows Hello for Business. Two assigned policies that set the same setting to a different value cause a Conflict in Intune, after which neither is applied; check-scope.js guards against that.
teksten.Zet Cached Exchange Mode aan voor de eig: Turns on Cached Exchange Mode for the user's own mailbox and keeps everything shared out of it: shared mail folders, shared calendars and Public Folder Favorites are not copied to the OST file.
teksten.Zet de advertentie-id uit, blokkeert het: Turns off the advertising ID, blocks the clipboard between devices, stops uploading user activities and keeps what the user types and speaks on the device.
teksten.Zet de cloudgestuurde inhoudsaanbeveling: Turns off Windows' cloud-driven content recommendations — the device part of the same OIB policy as Windows Spotlight.
teksten.Zet de generatieve AI-functies in Paint: Turns off the generative AI features in Paint and in Windows Settings: Cocreator, Image Creator, Generative Fill and the Settings Agent.
teksten.Zet de macOS-firewall aan en laat Gateke: Turns on the macOS firewall and lets Gatekeeper allow only software signed by an identified developer.
teksten.Zet de Microsoft Enterprise SSO-plug-in: Enables the Microsoft Enterprise SSO plug-in of Microsoft Authenticator, so that managed apps and Safari share a single Entra sign-in and the device can prove itself to Conditional Access.
teksten.Zet de verouderde NTLM-authenticatie uit: Turns off the outdated NTLM authentication in favour of Kerberos. Breaks old on-prem applications and devices that do not speak Kerberos — test first.
teksten.Zet de Windows Firewall aan voor het dom: Turns on Windows Firewall for the domain, private and public profiles and defines the default behaviour for inbound and outbound traffic.
teksten.Zet dezelfde Attack Surface Reduction-re: Sets the same Attack Surface Reduction rules as the blocking ASR policy to audit: Defender logs what it would stop, but stops nothing. Intended to measure the impact of a rule before you let it block.
teksten.Zet Google als standaardzoekmachine in E: Sets Google as the default search engine in Edge. An organisational decision, not a security setting.
teksten.Zet lokaal gewijzigde instellingen perio: Periodically resets locally changed settings to what Intune prescribes, so that manual tampering on a device is undone automatically.
teksten.Zet lokaal gewijzigde MDM-instellingen p: Periodically reverts locally changed MDM settings — the antidote to manual tampering on a device.
teksten.Zet meldingen op het vergrendelscherm en: Turns off notifications on the lock screen and AutoComplete in Internet Explorer.
teksten.Zet op een toestel met persoonlijk werkp: On a device with a personal work profile, sets a separate work profile code (six digits, medium complexity, locks after fifteen minutes, wipes only the work profile after ten attempts), blocks copying, sharing and screenshots from work to personal, and turns on Play Protect.
teksten.Zet op ingeschreven iPhones en iPads de: Turns off the generative Apple Intelligence features on enrolled iPhones and iPads — Writing Tools, Genmoji, Image Playground, Image Wand, personalised handwriting, summaries in Mail, Notes, Safari and Visual Intelligence — as well as the integration with external AI services such as ChatGPT.
teksten.Zet op Macs met Apple silicon een willek: On Macs with Apple silicon, sets a random, Intune-managed password on recoveryOS and the startup options, and replaces it every six months.
teksten.Zet Outlook in Online mode en verbiedt h: Puts Outlook in Online mode and prohibits creating an OST file, so that no mailbox content lands on the device's disk.
teksten.Zet Quick Machine Recovery aan: een appa: Turns on Quick Machine Recovery: a device that no longer boots fetches a recovery package from the cloud itself instead of waiting for a technician.
teksten.Zet Recall en Click To Do uit: Windows m: Turns off Recall and Click To Do: Windows then takes no screen captures of what happens on the screen and does not analyse them either.
teksten.Zet Siri uit met allowAssistant. Apple m: Turns Siri off with allowAssistant. Since macOS 26.4 Apple marks that key as deprecated, in favour of the declarative configuration com.apple.configuration.siri.settings (in Intune: sirisettings_sirisettings with sirisettings_enabled). It stays for now for the same reason as in [Baseline] - MAC - D - Apple Intelligence Restricted: that DDM configuration only exists from macOS 26.4 and only on supervised Macs, whereas this payload also works on macOS 14 and 15 and on a Mac the user enrolled themselves. [Baseline] - IOS - D - Restrictions Corporate already uses sirisettings (allowwhilelocked), because on iOS the old restriction applied differently. Switch over once the fleet is on 26.4 or later and enrolled via ADE.
teksten.Zet virtualisatie-gebaseerde beveiliging: Turns on virtualisation-based security, Credential Guard and memory integrity, so that credentials are held in an isolated part of memory. Requires a restart and can block old drivers.
teksten.Zet Windows Protected Print aan, verbied: Turns on Windows Protected Print, prohibits standard users from installing printer drivers for a shared printer, and shuts off printing over HTTP.
teksten.Zet Windows Spotlight, tips en consument: Turns off Windows Spotlight, tips and consumer-oriented suggestions, so that no advertisements or recommended apps appear on a work device.
teksten.Zet Windows-functies uit die bedrijfsdat: Turns off Windows features that can move business data outside or create noise, such as web search from the Start menu.
teksten.Zet zeven kleine CIS-gaten dicht in Wind: Closes seven small CIS gaps in Windows components: no automatic sign-in, no NTP server, no continuing on another device, no enumeration of local users, protected mode for the shell protocol, no WinRT access from hosted content and no upgrade offer via the Store.
teksten.Zonder assignment: ringen horen op een p: No assignment: rings belong on a pilot group, not on All Devices — that would contradict ring 3.
teksten.Legt de beveiliging van Google Chrome va: Locks down Google Chrome security to the same level as Edge: Safe Browsing on and impossible to bypass, malicious downloads blocked, certificate errors cannot be clicked through, and no company data to a personal Google account.
teksten.Google Chrome-beleid in de settings cata: Google Chrome policy in the settings catalog (chromeintunev1, chromeintunev141) — values chosen to match the Edge counterpart in this baseline; ids, options and ranges verified against DCv2/Settings in pl4nty/intune-change-tracking
teksten.Merkbaar voor wie Chrome gebruikt: aanme: Noticeable for Chrome users: browser sign-in, sync and saving new passwords are turned off. Remote debugging is turned off too, which breaks automated tests (Puppeteer, Playwright, Selenium) against the installed Chrome. Pilot group first.
teksten.Safe Browsing op standaard (1) en niet o: Safe Browsing on standard (1), not enhanced (2): enhanced sends every visited URL to Google. Download restriction 4 is 'block malicious downloads', the same value as in Edge. The password manager is turned off because Edge is the managed password manager; Chrome no longer saves new passwords, while passwords already saved keep working according to Google. Extensions have their own policy (Google Chrome Extensions), as with Edge; BlockExternalExtensions is here, because it only affects extensions that other software installs through the registry. ApplicationBoundEncryptionEnabled lives in the chromeintunev141 namespace in the catalog, the rest in chromeintunev1. Firefox has no settings catalog definitions: see IntuneTemplate/WIN/Remediations/firefox-policies.
teksten.Blokkeert extensies in Google Chrome, zo: Blocks extensions in Google Chrome, as Microsoft Edge Extensions does in Edge.
teksten.ExtensionInstallBlocklist '*' schakelt o: ExtensionInstallBlocklist '*' also disables extensions that are already installed, so every Chrome user loses their extensions. First check which ones are in use (Defender Vulnerability Management → Browser extensions) and put what is needed on ExtensionInstallAllowlist in a tenant-specific copy.
teksten.Apart van Google Chrome Security omdat d: Separate from Google Chrome Security because this is the policy that most often needs an exception: the rest of the Chrome hardening can roll out while the extension inventory is still running.
teksten.Zorgt dat een Chrome-update binnen drie: Makes sure a Chrome update takes effect within three days: relaunch notification required, forced relaunch outside working hours, and sooner when the version is badly out of date.
teksten.Google Update zelf (updatebeleid, kanaal: Google Update itself (update policy, channel) is not in the settings catalog: the `update~policy~cat_google~cat_googleupdate` definitions that do exist belong to the Edge updater, whose ADMX is a fork of Google Update that kept the old category names. As long as nobody turns updates off through Google Update, Chrome updates itself; this policy makes sure those updates actually take effect. RelaunchFastIfOutdated lives in the chromeintunev141 namespace, the rest in chromeintunev1. A device that is off at night only relaunches in the next window.
teksten.Voor een AI-beleid dat alle AI-tools ver: For an AI policy that prohibits all AI tools except Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Pro and GitHub Copilot for developers; without this policy nothing stops a user. NOTE when deploying: [Baseline] - WIN - U - Microsoft Edge User Experience sets the same block list. Two assigned policies with a different list cause a conflict, after which Intune applies neither. So copy this list into that policy, or remove it there — do not assign both. The three rules from OpenIntuneBaseline v4.0 are already included here — the Store website, the ms-windows-store:// protocol and javascript:// (against ClickFix) — so this list is complete. A URL block list is moreover friction, not a boundary: it does not work on a phone or on a personal device. The more robust variant is the Generative AI category in Defender Web Content Filtering; that lives in the Defender portal, not in this repo. **Alternative to [Baseline] - WIN - U - AI Usage Control Permitted**, which sets the same block list without the AI services. Assigning both results in a Conflict, and then nothing is blocked — not even the Store rules.
teksten.Staat over Bluetooth alleen muizen, toet: Allows only mice, keyboards, headsets, phones via Phone Link and passkeys over Bluetooth, and shuts off file transfer, tethering and serial connections.
teksten.Bluetooth CSP ServicesAllowedList (Micro: Bluetooth CSP ServicesAllowedList (Microsoft Learn, ServicesAllowedList usage guide) and the Bluetooth SIG Assigned Numbers — id and shape verified against DCv2/Settings in pl4nty/intune-change-tracking
teksten.Windows kan Bluetooth niet filteren op s: Windows cannot filter Bluetooth by type of device (iPhone, Android, brand), only by service: every UUID on the list is a Bluetooth profile that is allowed, and anything not on it stops working. The list is grouped in blocks, so you can remove or add a block per tenant. BLE basics (1800 Generic Access, 1801 Generic Attribute, 180A Device Information, 180F Battery, 1813 Scan Parameters, 1200 PnP Information) — never remove these; without these six, modern mice and keyboards drop out. Input: 1124 HID and 1812 HID over GATT (mouse, keyboard, pen, game controller). Classic audio: 1108/1112 Headset, 111E/111F Handsfree, 110A/110B/110D A2DP, 110C/110E/110F AVRCP. LE Audio for newer headsets and hearing aids: 1843–1855 (volume, microphone, audio streams, calls, media, Hearing Access). Phone via Phone Link: 111E/111F Handsfree (calls), 112E/112F/1130 PBAP (contacts), 1132/1133/1134 MAP (messages), and Apple ANCS 7905F431-… and AMS 89D3502B-… (notifications and media from an iPhone). Passkeys: FFF9 (phone as passkey via QR code) and FFFD (FIDO security key over Bluetooth). Deliberately not on the list, and therefore blocked: 1105 OBEX Object Push and 1106 OBEX File Transfer (sending files), 1115/1116/1117 PAN (tethering), 1101 Serial Port and 1103 Dial-up Networking. To allow file transfer, add 1105 and 1106 in a tenant-specific copy; to exclude phones, remove the phone block (keep Handsfree for headsets). Windows reads the list when the Bluetooth stack starts: after assigning or changing it, it only takes effect after a restart. Microsoft does not document whether the list also affects BLE advertisements the PC only receives (as with a passkey via QR code); FFF9 is on it to be safe. Sits next to [Baseline] - WIN - D - Wireless and Peripherals, no overlap: that one only turns off discoverability, this one decides which services work.
teksten.Bluetooth-bestandsoverdracht (OBEX) is e: Bluetooth file transfer (OBEX) is a route to get files onto and off a managed device past DLP, Defender and the proxy; tethering (PAN) is a network connection that bypasses the corporate network. The allowlist shuts both without touching the peripherals a user needs. An allowlist rather than a blocklist, because that is the only form Windows offers: a new profile added by Microsoft or a manufacturer is therefore closed by default.
teksten.Geldt voor elk Windows-apparaat met Blue: Applies to every Windows device with Bluetooth. The limit: devices that use a profile not on the list — a barcode scanner or measuring instrument over Serial Port (1101), a printer over Bluetooth — stop working. Such devices need a tenant-specific copy with that profile added.
teksten.Een allowlist zet alles uit wat er niet: An allowlist turns off everything that is not on it, and which Bluetooth devices are in use you only know once you look. In the pilot, test at least a mouse, a keyboard, a headset (classic and LE Audio), calling via Phone Link with an iPhone and an Android phone, and a passkey sign-in with the QR code. Only takes effect after a restart.
teksten.Zet de klok gelijk via NTP en laat gebru: Syncs the clock over NTP and lets users change the time zone, but does not turn on *Set time zone automatically*: the settings catalog has no setting for it. The OIB platform script Enable-AutoTimezone.ps1 in IntuneTemplate/WIN/PlatformScripts/ does that; assign it to all devices together with this policy.
